Om Namah Shivaya: Hindu mantra. Om Namah Shivaya (Devanagari: ॐ नमः शिवाय; IAST: Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya) is one of the most popular Hindu mantras and the most important mantra in Shaivism.
Known as 'Mr. Titanic' for his deep-sea expertise, this French explorer was among the five people killed when a submersible imploded near the famous wreck in June 2023 — who was he?
Paul-Henri Nargeolet: French naval officer and explorer (1946–2023)
Leader of Canada's Conservative Party and Official Opposition since 2022, this MP previously worked for Canadian Alliance leader Stockwell Day — who is he?
Nicknamed the 'Black Baron,' this scion of a Baltic German noble family became the last commander-in-chief of the White forces in southern Russia during the Civil War — who was he?

Houthi forces in Yemen have launched missiles and drones at shipping tied to Israel amid the Gaza war, drawing military responses from Israel, the US and the UK — what is this ongoing maritime conflict called?
Red Sea crisis: Houthi involvement in the Gaza war. The Red Sea crisis is an ongoing armed conflict and maritime crisis instigated by the Houthis, an armed group in Yemen.
Which retired Italian Army general, elected to the European Parliament for the League in 2024, founded his own far-right party called National Future in 2026?
Roberto Vannacci: Italian military officer and politician (born 1968)
Captain of the Shinsengumi's third unit during Japan's Bakumatsu period, this samurai later worked undercover as a Tokyo police officer under the alias Fujita Gorō — who was he?

Proclaimed in 1852 when a president crowned himself Napoleon III, this 18-year regime built out a national railway network even as historians later judged its foreign policy a failure — what was this government called?
Second French Empire: France under Napoleon III (1852–1870)
Currently Japan's Minister of Defense, this LDP lawmaker representing Kanagawa is the son of a former prime minister and once worked as his father's political secretary — who is he?
Married to the youngest sibling of King Charles III since 1999, this member of the British royal family previously worked in public relations before her wedding at Windsor Castle — who is she?
Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh: Member of the British royal family (born 1965)
He ruled an isolated pocket of Roman authority around Soissons long after the empire lost the region, until the Frankish king Clovis I defeated and killed him — who was this last Roman holdout?
Syagrius: 5th century Roman leader at Soissons.
Formed in 2015 as a reformation of a party once led by Jacques Chirac, this conservative party, inspired by Gaullism, saw its 2017 presidential candidate place third — which party?
This movement campaigns for women to have the same legal right as men to go bare-chested in public, and also supports mothers' right to breastfeed openly — which cause?
Topfreedom: Social movement to allow female toplessness.
Aboard a Soviet submarine during the Cuban Missile Crisis, this officer's lone veto blocked his two fellow commanders from launching a nuclear torpedo at U.S. ships — who was he?
Vasily Arkhipov: Soviet Navy vice admiral who prevented nuclear war (1926–1998)
Deeply in debt to Adolf Hitler for loans he'd borrowed, this aristocratic field marshal commanded Germany's army during the Battle of France and the invasions of Yugoslavia and Greece - who was he?
Walther von Brauchitsch: German Commander-in-Chief during World War II (1881–1948)
The first Canadian prime minister to hold a PhD, this Liberal racked up 21 years and 154 days in office across three non-consecutive terms — the longest tenure in the country's history; who is he?
William Lyon Mackenzie King: Canadian prime minister (1874–1950)
Claiming to be Catherine the Great's dead husband Tsar Peter III, this Cossack leader proclaimed an end to serfdom in 1773 and led a massive peasant uprising across the Volga-Ural region. Who was he?
Yemelyan Pugachev: Russian Cossack rebel leader (1742–1775)
Nicknamed 'The Acquitator' for his string of courtroom wins as a criminal defense lawyer, he served as France's Minister of Justice from 2020 to 2024 — who is he?
Éric Dupond-Moretti: French-Italian politician and lawyer (born 1961)
Which one below was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four. John Ray (29 November 1627 – 17 January 1705) was an English Christian naturalist and one of the earliest English parson-naturalists.
Which of these four is the eldest?

Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four. Omar Khayyam (1048–1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which of these four has been around longest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Paul Ehrenfest is a physicist. Suffering from depression, in 1933 Ehrenfest killed his disabled son, Wassik, and then himself.
Which of these is a chemist?
Karen Silkwood is a chemist. The company settled out of court for US$1.38 million, while not admitting liability.
What is the atomic number of Magnesium?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
In what year was Jean Tatlock born?
Jean Tatlock: Jean Frances Tatlock (February 21, 1914 – January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
In what year was Guglielmo Marconi born?
Guglielmo Marconi: In 1929, he was ennobled as a marquess (Italian: marchese) by King Victor Emmanuel III, thus becoming the 1st Marchese di Marconi.
In what year was Sam Altman born?
Sam Altman: Altman attended Stanford University for two years before he dropped out and co-founded Loopt, a smartphone geosocial networking service.
In what year did Ernest Lawrence die?
Ernest Lawrence: A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Coriolis force discovered?
Coriolis force: In physics, the Coriolis force is a pseudo-force that acts on objects in motion within a frame of reference that rotates with respect to an inertial frame.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Methotrexate: Pfizer. Methotrexate, formerly known as amethopterin, is a chemotherapy agent and immune-system suppressant.
Which country is Bombardier Global Express from?
Bombardier Global Express: Canada. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.
Who is credited with discovering Infrared?
Infrared: William Herschel. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Who is credited with discovering Cherenkov radiation?
Cherenkov radiation: Sergey Vavilov. A classic example of Cherenkov radiation is the characteristic blue glow of an underwater nuclear reactor.
Who is credited with discovering Argon?
Argon: William Ramsay. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.

A central nervous system stimulant of the phenethylamine class, this combo medication is approved for narcolepsy and ADHD — but is also taken as an appetite suppressant and cognitive enhancer. What is it?
Adderall is the brand name of a fixed-dose combination medication used for the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
These organic compounds, formed when one or more hydrogens in ammonia are replaced by carbon-based groups, are defined by their carbon-nitrogen bonds — what's this class of compounds called?
Amine (UK also) are organic compounds that contain carbon-nitrogen bonds.
NATO codenamed 'Curl' and nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR, this twin-engine turboprop transport was later license-built in China as the Xi'an Y-7 — what is it?

Antonov An-26 (NATO reporting name: Curl, nicknamed Nastia in the USSR) is a twin-engined turboprop regional airliner and military transport aircraft, designed and produced in the Soviet Union from 1969 to 1986.
Which genus of early hominins, which lived in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, gave rise to the genera Homo, Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus?
Australopithecus (-loh-; or, os-, from Latin australis southern 'grc' and (pthkos) ape) is a genus of early hominins that existed in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Biceps is a large muscle that lies on the front of the upper arm between the shoulder and the elbow.
Located in the head in most animals with nervous systems, this organ receives sensory information, generates thought and cognition, and coordinates the body's muscles and glands — name the organ?
Brain is an organ that serves as the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate and most invertebrate animals.
Caused by an overgrowth of a common yeast, this fungal infection is known as thrush when it affects the mouth and can also cause a genital yeast infection — name the condition?
Candidiasis is a fungal infection due to any species of yeasts in the genus Candida or those that were formerly classified in genus Candida but are now classified in the genus Candidozyma.
Also known by the taxonomic synonym Epilobium, this hardy perennial in the willowherb family is native throughout the temperate north — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.
Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

This naturally occurring but largely inactive steroid hormone shields organs like the kidneys from active cortisol, and gets converted back into cortisol by an enzyme mainly in the liver — what hormone is it?
Cortisone is a naturally occurring, mostly inactive pregnene (21-carbon) steroid hormone.
Known mostly through DNA evidence rather than abundant fossils, this extinct group of archaic humans ranged across Asia between roughly 200,000 and 32,000 years ago — what are they called?
Denisovan (d-(nz)) are an extinct species or subspecies of archaic human that ranged across Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene, approximately 200,000-32,000 years ago.
Sometimes called word blindness, this learning disability makes reading, writing, or speaking difficult despite a normal desire to learn, and often overlaps with ADHD — name the condition?
Dyslexia is a learning disability that affects either reading, writing, or speaking.
This tightly coiled duct sits behind each testicle, serving as the crucial link to the vas deferens where sperm mature before their onward journey — what is it?
Epididymis (pl.: epididymides or) is an elongated tubular genital organ attached to the posterior side of each one of the two male reproductive glands, the testicles.

Discovered in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb in 1952 and named for a pioneer of nuclear physics, element 100 is the heaviest that neutron bombardment can produce. Which synthetic element is it?
Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.

Discovered in Paris in 1875 and bearing the symbol Ga on the periodic table, this soft, silvery chemical element has such a low melting point — just below 30°C — that it turns liquid at warm room temperature. Name this element?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
Comprising about 50 species native to tropical regions worldwide, this genus produces roughly 80% of the world's natural fiber and doubles as an oilseed crop — which genus?
Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested.
In their healthy state these vascular cushions in the anal canal actually help with stool control — it's only when they swell or inflame that they earn the nickname "piles." What are they?
Hemorrhoid (or haemorrhoids), also known as piles, are vascular structures in the anal canal.
This negatively charged ion, one oxygen bonded to one hydrogen, acts as a base and forms industrially vital salts like the sodium version used to make millions of tons of chemicals. What ion is it?
Hydroxide (occasionally hydroxyl ion) is a diatomic anion with chemical formula OH.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.
This Liverpool-born mathematician roamed from finite groups to knot theory, but is best loved for inventing a famous cellular automaton called the Game of Life — who was he?
John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 - 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.

Named after the Italian word for lemon, this colorless liquid hydrocarbon is the main compound behind citrus peel fragrance, occurring mostly as a right-handed form extracted commercially by centrifugal separation or steam distillation - name the compound?

Limonene is a colorless liquid aliphatic hydrocarbon classified as a cyclic monoterpene, and is the major component in the fragrance and essential oil of citrus fruit peels, taking its name from Italian limone ("lemon").
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, quokkas, and tree-kangaroos among its 63 living species — what family is it?
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
First synthesized in 1982 near Darmstadt, this fleeting synthetic element of the periodic table's seventh period was named in 1997 after a pioneering Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist. What is it?
Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.

An Egyptian who studied architecture at Cairo University and worked as a civil engineer, this man was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta (September 1, 1968 - September 11, 2001) was an Egyptian engineer, architect, and the lead terrorist hijacker for al-Qaeda on American Airlines Flight 11.
This stocky Arctic whale carries a spiralled tusk up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to serve as weapon, tool, and sensor — what is it?
Narwhal (Monodon monoceros) is a species of toothed whale native to the Arctic.
Belonging to the beech family and encompassing about 500 species across the Northern Hemisphere, this hardwood tree or shrub bears a distinctive nut held in a small cup — name the tree?
Oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family.
This Felidae subfamily, first described in 1917 as covering only the big cats, later expanded to include the clouded leopard genus as well — which subfamily?

Pantherinae is a subfamily of the Felidae; it was named and first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 as only including the Panthera species, but later also came to include the clouded leopards (genus Neofelis).
A self-described socialist active in Finland's Pirate Party, this entrepreneur co-founded a famous file-sharing search engine and later started the privacy service Njalla — who is he?
Peter Sunde (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Derived enzymatically from a fatty acid found in nearly every tissue of the body, this class of lipid compounds produces diverse hormone-like effects despite not being true hormones — what are they called?
Prostaglandin (PG) are a group of physiologically active lipid compounds that have diverse hormone-like effects in animals.
Distinguished from its smaller relative the crow mainly by size, this large-bodied passerine bird genus includes the common and thick-billed species, the biggest passerines alive — what bird is it?
Raven is any of several large-bodied passerine bird species in the genus Corvus.
Created by Yukihiro 'Matz' Matsumoto in 1990s Japan, this dynamically typed programming language treats absolutely everything — even primitive data types — as an object — what's the language?
Ruby (programming language) is a general-purpose programming language designed with an emphasis on programming productivity and simplicity.
Made by Novo Nordisk and taken by injection or pill, this peptide medicine doubles as a diabetes treatment and a weight-management drug — what is it?
Semaglutide is an anti-diabetic medication used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, and an anti-obesity medication used for weight management.
This alkaline compound, commonly diluted in water and sold as household bleach, is derived from hypochlorous acid and is unstable in its pure anhydrous form. What is it?
Sodium hypochlorite is an alkaline inorganic chemical compound with the formula NaOCl (also written as NaClO).

Harvested from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, this bitter colorless alkaloid is infamous as a poison for rodents and birds — yet was once doled out in tiny doses to stimulate the heart and bowels. What is it?
Strychnine (-nin, US chiefly -nyne) is a highly toxic, colorless, bitter, crystalline alkaloid used as a pesticide, particularly for killing small vertebrates such as birds and rodents.
Sporting beaded antennae and a pale, soft-bodied worker caste, these decaying-wood eaters belong to the order Isoptera and are really highly derived cockroaches — what are they?
Termite are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.
These brightly colored Neotropical birds are known for their oversized, vividly patterned bills, and their chicks hatch completely naked with no down feathers at all — what bird is it?
Toucan are Neotropical birds in the family Ramphastidae.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
This mushroom genus contains the notorious 'death cap,' responsible for roughly 90% of all fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide — which genus?
Amanita: Genus of mushrooms. The genus is responsible for 95% of fatalities resulting from mushroom poisoning, with the death cap accounting for 90% of fatalities every year.
Consisting of a phenyl group attached to an amino group, this organic compound smells like rotten fish and serves as a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what is it called?
Aniline: Organic compound (C6H5NH2); simplest aromatic amine.
Its name comes from Greek roots meaning 'chief' and 'creator,' and historians often identify whole vanished civilizations by what survives of this visual art. What is it?
Architecture: Art and technique of designing buildings.

This rapid, irregular quivering of the heart's upper chambers can be entirely silent or bring palpitations and fainting — and it sharply raises the risk of stroke, dementia and heart failure. What is this arrhythmia?
Atrial fibrillation: Irregular beating of the atria of the heart.
Belonging to genus Fagus, this deciduous tree yields timber used for furniture, flooring, and plywood, and its wood also makes excellent firewood. What is this tree?
Beech: Genus of trees in the family Fagaceae.

Also nicknamed 'buffalo gnats' or 'turkey gnats,' these small biting insects in the family Simuliidae feed mainly on nectar, though females also drink blood from birds and mammals — what are they called?
Black fly: Family of insects. Black flies or blackflies (sometimes called buffalo gnats, turkey gnats, or white socks) are flies in the family Simuliidae of the Culicomorpha infraorder.
Also known as warble flies or gadflies, the larvae of which insect family live as internal parasites in mammal flesh or gut, with one species routinely infesting humans?
Botfly: Parasitic insect. Dermatobia hominis is the only species of botfly known to parasitize humans routinely, though other species of flies cause myiasis in humans.
Named from the Greek word for butter, this oily, foul-smelling compound with the formula CH3CH2CH2COOH is a key component of the mammalian gut. What is it?
Butyric acid: Chemical compound (CH3CH2CH2COOH). It is an oily, colorless liquid with an unpleasant odor.
These biomolecules often follow the tidy empirical formula (CH2O)n, and as polysaccharides like starch, glycogen, and cellulose they store energy and build structure — what family are they?
Carbohydrate: Organic compound that consists only of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Consisting mainly of the brain and spinal cord — and, surprisingly, the retina too — this part of the body integrates information to coordinate an animal's activity — what is it?
Central nervous system: Brain and spinal cord. The rest of this article exclusively discusses the vertebrate central nervous system, which is radically distinct from all other animals.
Sold as Thorazine, this drug was the first of the typical antipsychotics — used to treat schizophrenia and, oddly, hiccups that won't quit. What is it?
A shrub-like bush of western South America with oval leaves and small red berries, its leaves are chewed or brewed as a mild stimulant and famously contain a notorious alkaloid — which plant is it?
Coca: Plant in the Erythroxylaceae family.
This miniature Belgian-French dog breed comes in two varieties named for a butterfly and a moth, based on whether their ears stand erect or hang down — which breed?
Continental Toy Spaniel: Belgian and French breed of dog. The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.
Native to the Irano-Turanian region, this flowering plant's dried seeds season cuisines worldwide, despite no strong evidence backing its use in traditional medicine — which spice?
Cumin: Species of plant with seeds used as a spice.
Often tied to diseases like Alzheimer's, this incurable, progressive syndrome erodes memory, language, and motivation in stages — which condition is being described?
Sold under the brand name Motilium, this dopamine-blocking medication treats nausea and slow stomach emptying, but also raises prolactin levels — what is it?
This American astronomer proved that many so-called nebulae were actually separate galaxies, and in 1929 showed that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are — who is he?
Triggered by the parasympathetic nervous system and a rise in nitric oxide, this physiological event leaves an organ firm and engorged — what is it?
Erection: Physiological phenomenon involving the hardening and enlargement of the penis.

Also known as the wisent, this species is the heaviest wild land mammal on its continent — hunted to extinction in the wild by the early 20th century before being restored through captive breeding programs. Which animal?
European bison: Eurasian species of mammal. It is one of two extant species of bison, alongside the American bison.

Marked by widespread chronic pain plus fatigue and foggy thinking, this condition affects 2 to 4% of people, more often women, and was first recognised in the 1950s but only defined in 1990 — what is it?
Dubbed the "Flying Tailor," this inventor was so sure his wearable parachute would work that he leapt from the Eiffel Tower to test it himself — fatally. Who was he?
This scientific field measures Earth's precise shape, gravity, and orientation in space, underpinning satellite positioning systems and global mapping — which discipline?
Geodesy: Science of measuring the shape, orientation, and gravity of Earth.
This type of organ produces an organism's sex hormones and gametes — testicles in males, ovaries in females — what is it called?
Gonad: Gland that produces sex cells.
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
This natural anticoagulant boosts the activity of antithrombin and is used to prevent clotting during dialysis and in blood test tubes — what medication is it?
Heparin: Anticoagulant. Heparin, also known as unfractionated heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.

This American physicist dared to drop the wave-function-collapse postulate, proposing a 'relative state' theory that became the basis of the many-worlds interpretation — largely ignored until quantum decoherence vindicated him. Who is he?
Known as 'the father of modern optics,' this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote the influential 'Book of Optics' and proved that vision begins in the eye, not by rays leaving it — who is he?
Ibn al-Haytham: Arab physicist, mathematician and astronomer (c. 965 – c. 1040)
Awarded the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physics, this British scientist discovered in 1897 that cathode rays were made of what we now call electrons — who is he?

This American physicist worked with Niels Bohr on nuclear fission and had a gift for coinages — "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term that popularized "gravitationally collapsed objects." Who was he?
John Archibald Wheeler: American theoretical physicist (1911–2008)
Named from a Tongan and Marquesan word meaning 'bitter,' this pepper-family plant's ground root becomes a ceremonial Pacific Islands drink that numbs the mouth — what is it?
Kava: Species of plant. Kava or kava kava (Piper methysticum: Latin 'pepper' and Latinized Greek 'intoxicating') is a plant in the pepper family, native to the Pacific Islands.
Native to North America and infamous for occasionally eating their mates after reproduction, the females of this venomous spider species sport striking black-and-red coloring — what species is it?
Latrodectus mactans: Species of spider. Latrodectus mactans, known as southern black widow or simply black widow, and the shoe-button spider, is a venomous species of spider in the genus Latrodectus.
This big cat of the genus Panthera now ranges only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India, and is unusual among wild cats for living in social groups — what is it?
Lion: Large cat native to Africa and India.
Located near the backbone on either side of the heart, this organ extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide, driven mainly by the diaphragm — which organ is it?
Lung: Primary organ of the respiratory system.
This sugar alcohol pulls double duty as a low-calorie sweetener and a drug given by injection to lower pressure in the eyes or inside the skull — an osmotic diuretic. What is it?
Sold under the brand name Mobic, this NSAID in the oxicam family blocks COX-2 more strongly than COX-1 and ranked 27th among the most prescribed US medications in 2023. What drug is it?
A self-taught Soviet tinkerer who later became a lieutenant general, he designed a famously reliable assault rifle but felt sorrow at how widely it spread — who was he?

The tallest and heaviest living species of deer, this Northern Hemisphere giant is topped in North American body mass only by the bison, and its males sport broad, hand-shaped antlers unlike any other deer's pointed racks. What is it?
Moose: Largest species of deer. It is also the tallest, and the second-largest, land animal in North America, falling short only to the American bison in body mass.
Sold as Narcan, this opioid antagonist can restore breathing within minutes of an overdose but may trigger sudden withdrawal in opioid-dependent people — what is it?
Naloxone: Opioid receptor antagonist. Naloxone, sold under the brand name Narcan among others, is an opioid antagonist, a medication used to reverse or reduce the effects of opioids.
What is this — “Index of chemical compounds with the same name”?
Nitrogen oxide: Index of chemical compounds with the same name. Nitrogen oxide may refer to a binary compound of oxygen and nitrogen, or a mixture of such compounds:.

Sold under the brand name Zofran, this serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist prevents chemotherapy- and surgery-related nausea without the dopamine-blocking side effects that cause muscle restlessness — what is this drug?
Ondansetron: Medication to prevent nausea and vomiting.
Known for its fragrant leaves used to flavor dishes across Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and Hainanese cuisine, this member of the screwpine genus is prized in many Asian kitchens — which plant?
Pandanus amaryllifolius: Species of tropical plant.
Almost every member of this flightless, countershaded clan sticks to the Southern Hemisphere — except one lone species that creeps up to the equator in the Galapagos. What bird is it?
Penguin: Family of aquatic flightless birds.
With the formula H3PO4, this colorless, odorless compound is typically sold as an 85% aqueous solution and serves as a key ingredient in many fertilizers — what is it?
This plant process moves pollen from an anther to a stigma, eventually letting a tube grow down the style to reach the ovary and enable fertilization. What is it?
Pollination: Biological process occurring in plants.
Discovered in 1915, this red dwarf is the closest star to Earth besides the Sun, orbiting its two larger neighbors once every 550,000 years — which star?
Proxima Centauri: Nearest star to the Solar System.
Used to treat malaria resistant to chloroquine, this bitter compound also flavors tonic water and can cause ringing in the ears at high doses — what is it?
Quinine: Medication used to treat malaria and babesiosis.
Aristotle called this ancient art 'the faculty of observing the available means of persuasion,' identifying logos, pathos, and ethos as its three key appeals — which discipline?
Rhetoric: Art of persuasion. It is one of the three ancient arts of discourse (trivium) of classical antiquity, along with grammar and logic/dialectic.

Named after the naturalist who first studied it and described in 1797, this extremely venomous South Asian snake is notorious for its excruciatingly painful bite and ranks among the region's 'Big Four' — what snake is it?
Russell's viper: Species of venomous snake. Russell's viper (Daboia russelii) is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
Driven by an empirical cycle of observation, hypothesis, testing, and conclusion, this systematic discipline splits into natural and social branches. What is it?
Science: Systematic endeavour to gain knowledge.
